card.name: Zeibekiko
card.era: Late 17th-c. origin (Zeybek militia); popularized on the Greek mainland after 1922
card.profile: A solo, improvisational Greek folk dance related to the Turkish zeybek dance, named after the Zeybeks (irregular Aegean militia of the Ottoman Empire). First seen in the late 17th c. in Constantinople and Smyrna; originally a dance for two armed men, it became a solitary improvised dance. Rhythmic pattern 9/4 or 9/8. After the 1922 population exchange it spread on the mainland via laiko/rebetiko. Traditionally male and introspective (the 'eagle dance'), danced solo within a circle of seated, clapping companions; now also danced by women. Accompanied by bouzouki and baglamas (English Wikipedia; GTP Headlines).
card.insight: The zeibekiko was added to Greece's National Inventory of Intangible Cultural Heritage in March 2022 alongside the bouzouki, tzouras and baglamas; it is danced to rebetiko, the music genre UNESCO inscribed in 2017 (GTP Headlines, 24 Mar 2022).
